content: District Health Authorities in England and Wales were administrative units of the National Health Service (NHS) that operated between 1982 and 1996. These authorities functioned as a secondary tier of administration beneath the health regions. They replaced the Area Health Authorities, which were generally aligned with non-metropolitan counties, metropolitan boroughs, or groups of London boroughs, as well as the District Management Teams that managed hospitals on a daily basis. The two-tier administrative structure had been introduced in 1974. During the 1990s, the District Health Authorities underwent several reorganizations. In 1996, they were abolished and replaced by single-tier Health Authorities, which consolidated both the District and Regional levels of administration. Northern Region In 1982, sixteen District Health Authorities were established in the Northern Region, replacing nine Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1992 reduced the number of districts to fourteen. By 1994, the Northern Region became part of the larger Northern and Yorkshire Region, leading to further amalgamations: North Cumbria District was formed by merging East Cumbria and West Cumbria. South of Tyne District was created by combining Gateshead and South Tyneside. Tees District was formed by merging Hartlepool, North Tees, and South Tees. Morecambe Bay District (in the North Western Region) was created by combining South Cumbria and Lancaster. Yorkshire Region Seventeen District Health Authorities were created in the Yorkshire Region in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. Between 1991 and 1993, the number of districts was reduced to seven. In 1994, the Yorkshire Region merged with the Northern Region to form the Yorkshire and Northern Region. Trent Region In 1982, twelve District Health Authorities were established in the Trent Region, replacing eight Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1992 reduced the number of districts to eleven, with the creation of North Nottinghamshire District through the merger of Bassetlaw and Central Nottinghamshire Districts. In 1994, Lincolnshire District was formed by merging North Lincolnshire and South Lincolnshire. East Anglia Region Eight District Health Authorities were formed in the East Anglia Region in 1982, replacing three Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1992 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to six. In 1994, the East Anglia Region merged with the Oxford Region to form the Anglia and Oxford Region. During this time: East Norfolk District was created by merging Norwich District and part of Great Yarmouth and Waveney District in Norfolk. Waveney, located in Suffolk, was transferred to Suffolk District. North West Thames Region In 1982, the North West Thames Region's boundary was adjusted, transferring part of the City of Westminster to the North East Thames Region. This area was returned to the North West Thames Region in 1990. Additionally, the Borough of Spelthorne in Surrey was transferred from the South West Thames Region in 1982 but returned in 1993. Fourteen District Health Authorities were created in the North West Thames Region in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. Changes in central London districts occurred in 1985 and 1988: Riverside District was formed in 1985 by merging Hammersmith and Fulham with Victoria Districts. Parkside District was created in 1988 by merging Paddington & North Kensington with Brent Districts. In 1990, it expanded to include part of the City of Westminster from the abolished Bloomsbury District in the neighboring North East Thames Region. Parkside was later abolished in 1993, with parts transferred to Kensington Chelsea and Westminster, and others to Brent and Harrow. Reorganizations between 1992 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to nine. North East Thames Region In 1982, the North East Thames Region's boundary was adjusted to include part of the City of Westminster from the North West Thames Region. This area was returned in 1990. Fourteen District Health Authorities were created in the North East Thames Region in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. In 1990, Bloomsbury and Islington District was created, encompassing the London Borough of Islington and 11 wards from the London Borough of Camden. By 1993, it became part of Camden and Islington District. Reorganizations in 1990 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to seven. South East Thames Region Fifteen District Health Authorities were established in the South East Thames Region in 1982, replacing five Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1993 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to eight. South West Thames Region Thirteen District Health Authorities were created in the South West Thames Region in 1982, replacing five Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1993 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to ten. Wessex Region Ten District Health Authorities were formed in the Wessex Region in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1994 reduced the number of districts to six. In the same year, the Wessex Region merged with the South West Region to form the South and West Region. Oxford Region Eight District Health Authorities were created in the Oxford Region in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1993 reduced the number of districts to four. In 1994, the Oxford Region merged with the East Anglia Region to form the Anglia and Oxford Region. South Western Region Eight District Health Authorities were established in the South Western Region in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1991 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to five. In 1994, the South Western Region merged with the Wessex Region to form the South and West Region. West Midlands Region Twenty-two District Health Authorities were created in the West Midlands Region in 1982, replacing eleven Area Health Authorities. In 1993, North East Warwickshire District merged with South Warwickshire District to form Warwickshire District. Reorganizations between 1991 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to fifteen. Mersey Region Ten District Health Authorities were formed in the Mersey Region in 1982, replacing six Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1993 reduced the number of districts to seven. In 1994, the Mersey Region merged with the North Western Region to form the North West Region. North Western Region Nineteen District Health Authorities were created in the North Western Region in 1982, replacing eleven Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1994 reduced the number of districts. In the same year, the North Western Region merged with the Mersey Region to form the North West Region. Wales Nine District Health Authorities were established in Wales in 1982. Unlike England, Wales did not have Area Health Authorities, as the entire country was under the jurisdiction of the Welsh Office.
